force.title: The Graying Market
force.signature: The boomers hit their care years — demand floods into everything age-related, but reimbursement cuts and a caregiver shortage cap the upside.

A \u00b7 The body wears out: Aging joints and eyes drive implant and outpatient-surgery volume; robotics is now standard of care but Medicare cuts squeeze the price.
Hearing and vision decline create steady demand; OTC hearing aids and retail optical reshape who captures it.
Kidney and heart disease scale with age into recurring, consolidated, reimbursement-dependent care.
B \u00b7 Care leaves the hospital: Boomer demand meets a bed shortage and a wage spiral; PE rolls up the fragment.
The money rewards keeping seniors out of facilities; home care booms but can't hire fast enough.
Age-skewed outpatient specialties ride the demographic wave while fighting reimbursement pressure.
C \u00b7 The money side of aging: Living longer turns into an annuity and long-term-care market — the balance-sheet side of aging.
GLP-1 drugs are the biggest force in aging health — remaking weight loss, cardio-metabolic care, and pharma.
Wealthy, active retirees spend on experiences and the outdoors — a real growth pocket.
D \u00b7 The tensions: Medicare Advantage and insurers hold the purse; benefit cuts and cost control cap every provider's pricing.
The binding constraint isn't demand — it's the aides and nurses to serve it, and wages spiral.
E \u00b7 The big picture: Capstone: aging is a guaranteed demand wave, but labor and reimbursement decide who actually profits.
